name: Felis
body:
The felis are a cunning species of tribal warriors who worship the sun and moon. They are often identified by their bestial and cat-like features, sporting furry tails and large feline ears.

Felis Ancestral Traits
Size: Felis are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Type: Felis are humanoids with the catfolk subtype.
Base Speed: Felis have a base speed of 30 feet.
Keen Hearing: Felis’s large ears grant them increased hearing, gaining a +2 racial bonus to Perception when hearing.
Feline Tail: Felis have unparalleled balance and grace due to their cat-like features. This gives them a +2 racial bonus to Acrobatics to keep their balance or soften a fall.
Mischief: While not always true, felis are seen as mischief makers by other races. A felis selects any one combat maneuver, gaining a +1 racial bonus to CMB with and CMD against this selected maneuver. This choice can not be changed.
Low-Light Vision: Felis can see twice as far as a race with normal vision in conditions of dim light.
Languages: Felis begin play speaking Common and Catfolk. Felis with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following languages: Elven, Gnoll, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Lizzear, and Sylvan.
Racial Heritages

There are two distinct types of felis: solis or lunae, which each gain their own ability score adjustments and features.

Solis

Recognized by their darker skin and more colorful fur patterns, the felis of the sun are proud, strong warriors who live in small close knit communities. They tackle challenges with determination and ferocity.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Strength, +2 Constitution, -2 Charisma: Solis felis are strong and hardy, warriors who challenge and fight each other to be the best.
Impressive Strength: Solis often have surprising strength that surpasses their appearances. They gain a Dragon Thrust (Ex): At 3rd level, a dragon lancer learns to wield the skies as effectively as their mortal foes. They gain Branch Pounce as a bonus feat and as a full round action, a dragon lancer can make an Acrobatics check to jump before making a charge, which can trigger the Branch Pounce feat effect. When using Acrobatics in this way, dragon lancers are always counted as having a running start. This signature technique allows them to easily reposition around threats and obstacles, or use their extra momentum down on their enemies. Additionally, when using Acrobatics, the dragon lancer ignores fall damage equal to the height they successfully jumped. This replaces armor training 1 and armor mastery.
Spear Specialty (Ex): A dragon lancer must select Spears or Polearms with their weapon training.
Acrobatic Prowess (Ex): At 7th level, a dragon lancer’s jumping skills continue to improve. They add their level on all Acrobatics checks, and high jumps are no longer limited by their movement. Additionally, when a dragon lancer willingly falls, they take all falling damage as nonlethal and are never made prone after falling or missing a Branch Pounce attack. This replaces armor training 2.
Winged Glide (Ex): At 11th level, when jumping a dragon lancer can choose not to fall until the end of their next turn instead. This cannot be used in simultaneous turns until 15th level. At that point, they can maintain this ability for an additional simultaneous turn. This replaces armor training 3 and 4.
Natural Weapon: Solis possess two natural claws attacks that deal 1d4 damage.
Sturdy: Solis gain +1 hit point and gain an additional hit point for every 2 HD after their first.
Unburdened: Solis’s speeds are never modified by armor or encumbrance.
Lunae

Rarer, the felis of the moon are more insular and secretive. Their skin and fur colors are often dark or paler than their solar counterparts. The lunae are known for their cunning and cleverness and have adapted to living in caves and the underground.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Intelligence, +2 Wisdom, -2 Constitution: Lunae felis tend to solve their problems with their mind, sticking to the shadows rather than using brute strength.
Darkvision: Lunae’s eyes are adapted to see in the dark up to 60 ft.
Cunning Predator: Lunae gain a +2 racial bonus to Stealth and once per day can deal an additional 1d6 precision damage when attacking from stealth or with total concealment.
Natural Weapon: Lunae possess a natural bite attack that deals 1d6 damage.
Sprinter: Lunae gain a 10-foot racial bonus to their speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions.
